### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `b577112ce502dcd51f121f1737454ed6` · 2026-09-29T14:08:56Z

> The next M1 step is the gate (docs/plan/m1-separation.md, 'A kernel containment gate': one QEMU boot proving the kernel's primitives alone. Hostile code is preempted and ended at its deadline, a budget subtree is revoked with messages and lends in flight, and a victim stays responsive throughout. Kernel primitives only). K8, its last need, is finishing now. Please cut it into a package, GATE1, ready to launch when K8 merges:
> 1. What the boot runs: the hostile programs, the victim and what 'responsive' is measured against (reuse the sched-latency targets and the programs that exist, rather than new stand-ins, where they fit); which R and I rules each verdict proves; where each verdict comes from (rule F: the system, never the attacker). Say which existing cases it subsumes or leaves alone.
> 2. Whether it's a bench case, a set of cases or one composite boot. Widths: rv64 and rv32. Checked build or not.
> 3. The page delta: where the gate's evidence is written (a section on the M1 plan page, or on docs/kernel/README.md), and its status line.
> 4. The package node GATE1 (package, parent M1, Tier A, size), needing K8, with the gate step needing GATE1 or folded into it, whichever is cleaner.
> 5. The implementer's reading list, owned paths and traps in .wash/local/GATE1-implementer.md.
> If a design choice is the owner's, say so. Commit the page text as planned, with the owner's sign-off, staged by path, and reply on this thread.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `9f8af3d896487628ef3d004118e14992` · 2026-09-29T14:16:20Z

> GATE1: the kernel containment gate
> 
> 1. Sign off the gate as written (uncommitted) in docs/kernel/README.md#containment? One composite boot, bench:kernel-containment, rv64+rv32, one hart, checked build, virtual time, tracing kernel, pinned seed from a 16-seed sweep. One launcher (sole program, owns console and reset) starts the latency workload's driver and steward stand-ins, a victim server and a bystander; the steward stand-in runs two hostile leases at a time (8 ended by deadline, 8 by its decision). Each hostile agent spins without entering the kernel, enters it in a tight loop, parks lent calls and blocked sends at the victim through lease-stamped handles, runs a sub-agent budget with its own later deadline, and fills its lease and handle table (MAX_HANDLES). Verdicts come from kernel exit notices, the victims, budget_usage, the kernel trace and the oracle, never a hostile agent. Targets are responsiveness's; the gate adds none. It keeps every focused case.
>    - Approve (recommended): Commit the page text as planned; GATE1 launches when K8 merges.
>    - Change it: Say what to change.
> 2. The hostile agent fills its lease and handle table to make R10's walk as long as a lease of its size can. docs/todo/budget-destroy-cost.md says R10's cost is near its target (39 ms, notice 54 ms), so the gate may miss R10, the deadline notice or a lease's end. If it does, what happens?
>    - Stop, fix R10 first (recommended): GATE1 stops at the miss and reports it with the sweep. budget-destroy-cost (planned under the steward step) moves forward as its own Tier A kernel package ahead of the gate, and GATE1 lands after it. No target is widened and the hostile agent is not weakened.
>    - Fold the fix into GATE1: GATE1 also makes R10's cost follow the dying subtree. The package gets larger and mixes bench and kernel work.
>    - Fix R10 before GATE1 anyway: Build budget-destroy-cost now, before GATE1, whether or not the gate would miss.
>    - Set gate-only targets: Set the gate's own targets from its sweep. This widens what counts as responsive; not recommended.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `00d02fe266dbf93432b3a83a1bf3eb9d` · 2026-09-29T14:20:08Z

> Answered, owner signed off. Page text committed on redoubt, a926fd1c3 (docs/kernel/README.md, docs/plan/m1-separation.md; staged by path; doccheck clean).
> 1. What runs, rules, verdict sources: docs/kernel/README.md#containment (verdict table: R10, deadlines, R21, R3, I15, I9, R9, I2, I10, R12, I14). The launcher is the sole program on sched::Bench. It runs the latency workload's driver and steward stand-ins, a victim server and a bystander. The steward stand-in keeps two hostile leases live, 8 ended by deadline and 8 by decision. The hostile agent's threads are listed on the page. Every verdict comes from the kernel's notices and trace, the victims, budget_usage and the oracle. Targets are Responsiveness's (K8's new numbers once merged); the gate adds none. It subsumes no case; budget-deadline, redoubt-revoke, uaf-lent-page, endpoint-destroy-open-calls and sched-latency all stay. It closes the Deadlines/timer tight-loop gap.
> 2. One composite boot case, bench:kernel-containment. rv64+rv32, one hart, checked build, icount, sched-trace plus the oracle post-check, pinned seed from a 16-seed sweep.
> 3. Evidence goes in the new section docs/kernel/README.md#containment, Status: planned · M1. The M1 page gains a Kernel cases row ('not yet'), and the gate bullet links to the section.
> 4. Nodes: GATE1 is a package under M1, needs K8, Tier A, size M. The gate step now also needs GATE1; I kept the step because this thread is attached to it.
> 5. .wash/local/GATE1-implementer.md.
> Owner decisions: approve as written. On a miss of R10, the deadline notice or a lease's end, GATE1 stops and docs/todo/budget-destroy-cost.md moves forward as its own kernel package first; no target is widened and the attacker is not weakened.
